svg.title: AOD-9604: what has actually been tested
svg.desc: AOD-9604: what has actually been tested. Fat loss in obese rodents (2000-2001): Cut body-weight gain in obese rats and mice in early lab studies. Verdict: Shown in animals. Does it act like growth hormone?: No GH-receptor binding or high blood sugar in mice; no IGF-1 rise in trials. Verdict: Reportedly no. How it works: Lipolysis signal in animals; FDA says the target is still unknown. Verdict: Unknown. Weight loss in people, small trials: Single-dose and 1- to 4-week trials, IV and oral. Verdict: Not significant. Weight loss in people, phase 2b (2007): 502 people, 24 weeks, oral; company ended the obesity program. Verdict: Primary endpoint missed. Cartilage repair: One rabbit study of knee injections. Verdict: Animal only. Injected under the skin, as sold today: FDA found no human data for this route. Verdict: No human data. FDA review for compounding (2024): Advisers voted 0-12 against listing; nomination since withdrawn. Verdict: Not allowed. Approved drug or sport-legal: No FDA-approved product; banned in sport as a GH fragment. Verdict: Neither.
